hook.line: "SEO is dead." Answer engine optimization is how you get found in ChatGPT, Claude and Perplexity.
hook.visual: Close selfie shot, mouth open mid-word; white boxed title 'SEO Is Dead. 3 Websites For AI Search Engines' over a big word caption with a red highlight.

beats.what: Bold claim spoken over a boxed title that also promises a list of 3 websites.
Sets up the frame: stack these three websites together to dominate every search result.
First cut (after a 14.9 s opening shot) to a phone-filmed laptop screen showing site one, ranked.ai.
Tool dashboard filmed on the laptop while he explains what it optimises.
Back to face to name site two, Syllaby.io, keyword highlighted in the caption.
Screen footage of the video tool with a stock b-roll clip of someone at a laptop.
Content calendar grid: a month of scheduled videos.
Face again for the third stack: a Reddit reply bot.
Automation flow diagram filmed on screen as he says it auto-responds to threads.
Payoff: dominate every platform, which is what trains the AI models; then 'save this'.

why_it_works: 'SEO is dead' contradicts what the target viewer does for work, and the title adds a concrete list of 3, so the claim has a promised payoff.
'Stack' framing makes each tool a step in one system, so viewers wait for all three instead of leaving after the first.
Cuts to the real tool screen at every name (11.8 cuts/min after the first) prove each site exists, which drives the 'save' behaviour (2,208 shares on 106k plays).
weaknesses: First 14.9 s are one unbroken shot before any visual proof appears.
Screen shots are a phone filming a laptop: small, glare-prone UI that is hard to read.
The middle tool is his own product, so the 'list' doubles as an ad, which can cost trust.
for_robert: Copy the 'stack' structure: name tool one, cut to its real screen, return to face for tool two. Fred could stamp a '1/3', '2/3', '3/3' badge on each screen cut, so the first proof arrives sooner than 15 s.
